summary: Sends camera tracking, lens, and timecode channel data over the network using the Stype HF protocol, allowing TouchDesigner to emulate or feed a Stype camera-tracking source.
key_concepts: Stype Out CHOP is a TouchDesigner Pro operator for sending camera tracking, orientation, lens, and timecode data over Stype HF.
It can emulate a physical Stype camera or feed another device or program that processes Stype tracking data.
Packets are sent once per frame from the current CHOP input channel values.

Expected input channels include recording, focus_distance, packet_number, hour/minute/second/frame timecode, transform, FOV, aspect, focus/zoom, sensor center, radial distortion, and sensor size values.
If an expected input channel is absent, the operator sends a default value, so missing channel names can look like valid but wrong tracking data.
Timecode can be referenced from a CHOP, DAT, or Timecode object, and packet numbers can either auto-increment each frame or come from an input channel.

common_gotchas: Official docs list this operator as TouchDesigner Pro only.
Packets are sent once per frame from current input CHOP channels.
If an expected channel is absent, Stype Out sends a default value, which can hide upstream naming mistakes.
Input channels include recording, focus_distance, packet_number, timecode, camera transform, FOV, aspect, focus/zoom, sensor center, distortion, and sensor size values.
Use Timecode Object/CHOP/DAT when timecode should come from a trusted source rather than input channels.
Protocol, destination address, port, and local NIC must match the receiver.
